newsitem.title: USA: SABRE Group boosts IPO price range to $25-$27.
newsitem.headline: SABRE Group boosts IPO price range to $25-$27.

text.p: Sabre Group Holdings Inc has boosted the estimated price range for its proposed initial public offering to $25 to $27 a share, from its previous range of $20 to $23, according to a regulatory filing.

The change means the IPO will raise roughly $525 million. SABRE, the computer reservations and information subsidiary of AMR Corp, will become one of the 10 largest computer service firms in terms of market capitalization after the IPO, which analysts say will be one of the hottest deals this week.
Goldman Sachs is the lead underwriter of the offering of 20.2 million shares.
The offering will go to market sometime this week.

The company owns the SABRE system, a real-time transacton processing systems which operates from an underground computer facility in Tulsa, Oklahoma to over 120,000 computer access terminals around the world.

Standard & Poor's recommends the deal, according to a research report. It gives the deal an initial price target of range $27 to $30 based on valuing the company in comparison to other transaction-oriented firms like First Data Corp, and to other information technology services firms like Electronic Data Systems Corp and Computer Sciences Corp.
